kurzbeschreibung: The Achensee is Tirol’s largest lake—turquoise-blue waters framed by steep mountain slopes, famous as the "Sea of the Alps".
beschreibung: The Achensee is located in the triangle between Innsbruck, Kufstein, and Bavaria, and with an area of 6.8 km², it is the largest lake in Tirol. Its crystal-clear, turquoise water reaches temperatures of up to 25°C in summer—ideal for swimming, sailing, surfing, and diving. The lake is surrounded by the steep walls of the Karwendel and the Brandenberger Alpen. The main towns, Achenkirch and Pertisau, offer direct lakeside access, family-friendly hotels, and numerous mountain railways. In winter, the Christlum ski area in Achenkir beckons. Since 1887, the Achenseeschifffahrt has connected the towns with historic steamships.
tipps: The Achensee Railway is a historic steam cog railway from Jenbach to the lake – a nostalgic adventure.
The Achensee panoramic trail runs for about 40 km all the way around the lake.
The Karwendel on the western shore is one of the largest nature parks in Austria.
empfehlungen: A must: A ride with the Achensee-Schifffahrt from Pertisau to Achenkirch – the turquoise waters surrounded by the steep Karwendel mountains are unforgettable. Afterwards, stop by the Seehotel Einwaller for Austrian classics with a view of the lake.
umgebung: The Achensee is located in the northeast of Tirol, nestled between the Karwendel (west) and the Brandenberger Alpen (east). To the north, the region borders Bayern (Syrienstein), and to the south, it meets the Inntal (Jenbach). Nearest towns: Jenbach (10 km), Schwaz (20 km). The Achenseebahn connects the lake with the Inntal.
